why: Reject-to-null dropped, so `?menuTransition=swoosh` becomes a `MenuTransition` the HUD then turns into `.hud--menu-transition-swoosh` -- a class matching no rule, which renders as the SHIPPED transition while the flag reports the treatment as active. That is the failure mode the whole registry's reject-to-null idiom exists for (`backdrop`, `mineWarn` and `blockedFire` all state it), and adoption sharpened it: the silent fallback used to be the old crossfade and is now the new default, so a mistyped `fade` observes exactly the behaviour it was typed to rule out. Scoped to menu-transition.test.ts, whose parser case sweeps the four registered names and then five rejected spellings including a case variant and a space form.
killedBy: menuTransition: the flag that names a transition accepts every name in the vocabulary and nothing else -- population: the 4 registered names
